dev_brackets: Write Python function balanced(s) that returns True exactly when round parentheses in s are balanced. Ignore all other characters. A closing parenthesis before its matching opener is invalid. Return only the function, with no examples or prose.
heldout_prime: Return only Python function is_prime(n). It must return a bool saying whether integer n is prime; negative numbers, zero and one are not prime. Do not import anything. No Markdown, examples or explanation.
heldout_rle: Return only Python function runs(xs) which groups consecutive equal values into a list of (value, count) tuples. Empty input returns an empty list. Values may be lists, so do not require hashing. No imports, Markdown, examples or explanation.
heldout_dedup: Return only Python function unique_in_order(xs) that removes duplicates anywhere in the input while preserving the first occurrence of each value. Elements can be unhashable lists or dictionaries. Empty input returns an empty list. No imports, Markdown, examples or explanation.
heldout_json: Return exactly one JSON object, no Markdown, with keys project, retries, active, tags. Project is willow, retries is zero, active is true, and tags is an array containing red then blue. Do not add any keys.
new_lower: Return only Python function lower_bound(xs, target), with no Markdown, imports, examples or explanation. xs is a sorted list of integers, possibly empty or containing duplicates. Return the first index i with xs[i] >= target, or len(xs) if none. Use binary search in O(log n) time.
new_merge: Return only Python function merge_intervals(intervals), no Markdown, imports, examples or explanation. Each interval is a pair (start, end) of integers with start <= end. Input may be unsorted. Merge overlapping or touching intervals and return sorted (start, end) tuples. Empty input returns []. Do not modify the input.
new_chunks: Return only Python function chunks(xs, k), no Markdown, imports, examples or explanation. For list xs and positive integer k, return consecutive slices of at most k elements, as a list of lists. Keep the final shorter slice; empty xs returns []. Do not modify xs.
new_moving: Return only Python function moving_sums(xs, k), no Markdown, imports, examples or explanation. xs is a list of integers and k is positive. Return the sum of each consecutive window of exactly k elements, in order. If len(xs) < k return []. Use O(len(xs)) time and do not modify xs.
